thread:
incident-bot: Paging: @oncall — Sev2 API latency spike (us-east1) detected (error_rate < 10% but 95th latency > 2.5s) 1765000000

Leah R: I got the page, jumping on it. Any quick context?

Dinesh P: Seeing a sudden tail in decoder shards, looks like a KV cache thrash. Rolling averages for active sessions spiked around 1764999900.

Alex M: Confirmed. Metric dashboards show request_q depth increased by 3x for the t3g serving pool. No recent deploys in that pool.

Maria S: Tagging the customer-impact tracker — I see a handful of 503s from the old fallback path when latency exceeded threshold. Short customer-facing blips for chat sessions.

Leah R: Good catch. Dinesh, can you try a soft restart of the affected inferencer workers? I'll place a temporary rate-limit on non-critical routes to reduce pressure.

Dinesh P: Doing soft restart of shard group 4 now:```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inferencer-shard-4 -n us-east1-serving
```

incident-bot: Deploy job started by Dinesh P — rollout id 7a3f. Progress updates posted.

Sam T: I'll flip traffic lowering for the embeddings route for 5m to relieve the pool:```
redwoodctl traffic set --route /v1/embeddings --region us-east1 --weight 0.1
```

Alex M: Restart finished, nodes rejoined. 95th latency dropped to ~1.1s within two minutes. Request queue back to normal.

Maria S: Customer impact note: SOC ticket #4201 — chat sessions experienced 10-20s stalls for ~8 minutes. I'll send an update noting transient degradation.

Leah R: Thanks team. This looks mitigated. Let's run the post-incident checklist: assign postmortem owner, decide on monitoring changes, and schedule the postmortem. Who can own the writeup?

Dinesh P: I can take postmortem owner. Will cover root cause (cache eviction pattern), immediate mitigation, and long-term fixes.

Sam T: I'll own alert tuning and paging policy changes. We should reduce noisy paging from the 95th-latency alert that fires on small transient blips.

Alex M: I can pick up the runbook update for shard restarts and include the `redwoodctl traffic` knob examples.

incident-bot: Action items created: PM-318 (postmortem doc), OPS-719 (alert tuning), DOC-412 (runbook update). Due dates suggested as 3 days, 5 days, 2 days respectively.

Leah R: Scheduling postmortem slot — propose tomorrow 09:30 PT. If that works, Dinesh/Sam/Alex please RSVP.

Dinesh P: Approved. I can present the logs and the KV cache eviction graphs.

Sam T: Works for me. I'll bring an alerting proposal: change 95th-latency rule to require sustained >2.5s for 3m and add a burst suppression window. Also add a secondary signal: queue depth > x.

Alex M: +1. Also we should add a metric-based cooldown on canary/rollback automation when queue depth rises unexpectedly.

Maria S: I'll prepare the customer impact summary and communication template for the SOC.

Leah R: Nice. For remediation, Dinesh, do you think we need a code change (KV cache eviction policy) or infra config (bigger cache/slot) first?

Dinesh P: Short-term: increase KV cache memory limit on the worst-hit pods and tune eviction threshold (config change). Long-term: change cache eviction to be workload-aware and add telemetry on eviction spikes (code + metrics). I'll include both in the postmortem.

Sam T: For alerting improvements, proposed items: 1) Convert a single 95th-latency page into a composite alert (95th-latency sustained AND queue depth), 2) Add per-route rate-of-change suppression to avoid noisy pages from sudden legitimate traffic bursts, 3) Add a post-alert auto-snooze when mitigation runbooks are triggered.

Leah R: Those sound reasonable. Let's also document expected customer thresholds and SLO implications — Maria, can you confirm which customers got affected and whether any are enterprise customers?

Maria S: One mid-market customer had repeated stalls, no enterprise contracts impacted. I'll flag in postmortem and include remediation comms.

incident-bot: Postmortem meeting scheduled: 1765085400 (tomorrow 09:30 PT). Calendar invites sent to participants.

Leah R: Quick follow-ups:
- Dinesh: PM-318 assigned to you, due EOD +3 days.
- Sam: OPS-719 alert tunings, due EOD +5 days.
- Alex: DOC-412 runbook edits, due EOD +2 days.
- Maria: Customer note and SOC entry, due EOD +1 day.

Dinesh P: Acknowledged. I'll attach the eviction heatmap and heap profiles to the doc.

Sam T: I'll draft alert thresholds and the suppression config, will post in the runbook PR for review.

Alex M: Will add the `redwoodctl` troubleshooting steps and an ordered checklist.

Maria S: Drafting the SOC message now.

Leah R: One more item — we should add an automated smoke test that exercises the slow path and measures 95th latency after deploys to this pool. Can the infra team add a synthetic job?

incident-bot: New task INFRA-921 created for synthetic smoke tests.

Dinesh P: Sounds good. I'll also instrument eviction counters per shard and set up a dashboard panel pinned in the incident pager.

Leah R: Great work everyone. I'll close the incident when postmortem doc is published and actions are triaged.

Alex M: Closing notes: learned that cache thrash can manifest without deploys and that queue depth is a better early signal.

Sam T: Agreed. Paging policy next steps noted.

Maria S: Sending SOC update now.

incident-bot: Incident marked resolved by Leah R at 1765000605.

Leah R: Thanks all. See you at the postmortem. :thumbsup:
